precepts.text: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation. They feared Rome; the princes of the world feared Rome. That was their god.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Paul says the princes of this world did not know the hidden wisdom, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” John shows why: “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

If they left him alone, everybody was going to believe on him. But they feared Rome. The princes of the world feared Rome, and that was their god. They could see the miracles and still chose their place and their nation under Rome over the Son of God.

That is why the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid from such men. The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome; had they followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right. But they said, no, we follow Rome, and so they crucified the Lord of glory.

precepts.text: Many of the Jews which had seen the things which Jesus did believed on him: they saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead. But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done. You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God. Those same evil spirits are around today.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Here is another example of the evil of these people: “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead.

But watch the next verse: “But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God: I'm going to tell the scribes and Pharisees what Christ done did.

If I saw Christ raise somebody, I'm at his hip. I'm not leaving his side. I'm with him forever. I'm not running to them down yonder.

Them people back then, those same evil spirits are around today. Some see the truth with their own eyes and still go running to the men they have made their heads, the scribes and Pharisees, instead of holding to Christ. That is the voluntary humility and worshipping of men in Colossians 2:18: giving yourself over to men who are enemies of God, and being beguiled of your reward.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
John 11 shows the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod at work. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They believed on Christ.

“But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” Wherever there is good, evil has to be there. You had the believers, and then you had coons set up there, running to tell.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans. That lets you know who their masters were and who they were following after. That is the leaven of Herod.

Leaven is an influence that spreads. That bitterness is on the inside, and it corrupts the spirit, the same bitterness that was in Cain toward Abel. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead to keep their place under Rome. If you are bitter toward your brother, you are in the same position as the scribes and Pharisees: the same spirit.

precepts.text: Are there not twelve hours in the day? What the white man has done is daylight savings time, where they change time forward or backward. They play with times.
precepts.point: And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time: time is singular, times is plural, and the dividing is the half; that is three and a half, as Revelation explains.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.” Christ says there are twelve hours in the day.

What the white man has done is make something called daylight saving time, where they move time forward or backward. They play with times. Daniel said this man would “think to change times and laws”, and here is one more way he has done it: even the hours of the day are shifted at his word.

God set the day by his light; man changes the clock. That is one of the times the fourth kingdom has changed on the whole world.

precepts.text: Caiaphas: it is expedient that one man die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Both kingdoms were condemned under the covenant they kept violating, and that is the curse of the law Christ died to take us out of.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Caiaphas points out what the curse of the law is. “And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.”

Why would the whole nation perish? Because they were under the old covenant that they agreed to and kept violating over and over again. The northern kingdom went off first, and the southern kingdom fell right after, and both were destroyed by the nations. Standing in the old covenant, based on our own actions and on the law and the prophets, both kingdoms were condemned. By default both were under the curse of the law, which is condemnation. They should have been destroyed.

But the Lord had other plans. He said, I will not destroy them; I love them; I am going to have my son go and die for them, and redeem them from the curse they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27, where all the people said Amen. That is Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse and death are the same thing; being made a curse for us means he was killed for us. Christ died to take us out of that contract and put us into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, the northern kingdom.

precepts.text: Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said it is expedient that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not, and prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation, and not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. The curse of the law is death on the whole nation; Christ took it on himself for Judah and for Israel scattered abroad, the ones Paul went to among the Gentiles.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.” Some people read right past that. What is the curse of the law? Death. But you need a scripture to back up what you say, and John 11 is it.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation, all twelve tribes, perishing: that is the curse of the law. All twelve tribes broke the first covenant, and by that default we were all worthy of death. When Christ died, he took that curse upon himself for us. That is “being made a curse for us”: dying for us.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only.” Not for Judah only, “but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Gather together in one is reconciliation, at-one-ment, atonement.

So Christ died for Judah and for Israel, all twelve tribes. Those scattered abroad are the ones Paul was going to among the heathen, among the Gentiles, while being called Gentiles themselves. That is how “the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”

precepts.text: The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come and take away our place and nation. Caiaphas said it is expedient that one man die for the people. The pastors cannot speak the truth because the white man would take their platforms and make them commoners.
precepts.point: That is the church blitz in the Bible. Our own people will persecute the prophets who bring them the truth, in their churches, which is where we have to go. We arrive with the same Bible they have and they put hands on us and pull guns, with the love of Jesus.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Why would the rulers of the synagogues kill and crucify the prophets sent to them? John 11 shows what was in their hearts. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

That is the problem. It is not that they could not see the truth; it is their place. The same holds for the pastors today: if they speak the truth, the white man is going to take away their place, their riches and their platforms and make them into commoners. They do not want that, so they have to follow Rome. They have to follow America's doctrines. They cannot speak the truth.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The one man is Christ. Better to kill him than lose their position.

So when we come into the churches with the same Bible they have, and they put hands on us and pull guns on us with the love of Jesus, it is the same spirit: the prophets are scourged in the synagogues to protect the place of the rulers.

precepts.text: Caiaphas prophesied that it was expedient one man die for the people, that the whole nation perish not; and not for that nation only, but that he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. Even the evil high priest saw both kingdoms gathered.
precepts.point: I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice, and there shall be one fold and one shepherd. Christ is of Judah, so 'this fold' is the southern kingdom and the other sheep are the northern kingdom, brought in through Judah's teaching, fulfilling Hosea 1 and Ezekiel 37.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said, “I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. Christ is of Judah, so this fold is the southern kingdom, and the other sheep are the northern kingdom. “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice”, through the teachings of Judah first, “and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd”: one head, one king, as Hosea 1 and Ezekiel 37 said.

The Lord moved even the high priest, as stupid and evil as he was, to see it too. “And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation is all of us, all twelve tribes; Christ did not die for one kingdom only.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” The children of God scattered abroad are the ones Peter wrote to in 1 Peter 1: the northern kingdom. He gathered both kingdoms together as one.

So Caiaphas, who hated the Messiah, prophesied the same thing Christ said: other sheep not of this fold, brought into one fold. The builders were appointed to reject Christ, because by rejecting him they would have him killed, and by being killed he would grant the northern kingdom a chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold.

precepts.text: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come and take away our place and nation.
precepts.point: Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. They answered, we were never in bondage. Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
When Christ told them “the truth shall make you free”, they answered, “We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” That's what the creature comfort negroes and the content creators say: I'm not in bondage, I make money, I own four cars and a bunch of real estate; y'all negroes is playing victim. But “Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” Sin and captivity go hand in hand. Even if you think you're free, you're captive in your mind: celebrating New Year's, Thanksgiving and Christmas, you're still a slave, and we've been there so long we have no idea we're in captivity at all.

Watch what the same rulers said among themselves. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles.” “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” If we leave him alone to teach, they'll leave us and go to him.

That is the proof: they knew they were in bondage. In front of the people they fronted, acting tough: we ain't in bondage. But they answered to the Romans, and behind closed doors they admitted the Romans could take away their place and nation.

It's the same thing today. Publicly they call us a cult, say we hate everybody, say we're racist. Behind closed doors: these guys are changing lives, people are leaving the church, they're growing, they're dangerous, influential, charismatic, orderly, militant, uniform; we've got to do something about these guys. You always have people making a covenant with hell and death, then and now.

precepts.text: The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him thus alone, the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation; men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer.
precepts.point: The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

precepts.why:
The officers of the children of Israel cried unto Pharaoh, and his answer was, “Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the Lord.” The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now.

The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” Men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer. The officers did see that they were in evil case: no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them, and deliverance was not coming from Egypt.

precepts.text: If we let him thus alone the Romans shall come; the same spirit feared the oppressor more than the Most High.
precepts.point: In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians”; “it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.” Serving the slave master felt easier than having faith in the Most High, and the same spirit was in Israel in the days of Christ.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” They confessed he did many miracles, and still their fear was the Romans. The fear of the oppressor outweighed belief in the miracles, the same as at the sea, where the Egyptians marching outweighed everything the Lord had done in Egypt.

That is the same word our people speak today: why are you stirring up trouble, why tell us to come out of the ways of Babylon; let us alone to serve the slave master.

precepts.text: The council fears the Romans will take their place and nation, and Caiaphas says it is expedient one man die for the people, and to gather in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
The council feared that “the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” Caiaphas told them, “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.”

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Caiaphas spoke from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms, not of himself.

That nation he must die for is Israel. Not for that nation only means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.
